title: GCS configuration document
description:
The storage gateways, collections and endpoint roles for one Globus Connect Server endpoint. Terraform renders this with `jsonencode` into /<prefix>/globus/config; the on-instance reconcile reads it; `globus doctor` checks it.

THIS SCHEMA IS NOT THE WHOLE CONTRACT. It states the structural rules only. The rule that actually catches mistakes is referential — a collection naming a gateway that is not declared, or a role scoped to a collection that is not declared — and JSON Schema cannot express it. `globus_admin.configdoc.validate()` is authoritative and checks both; it is stdlib-only so the reconcile can use it on the instance. This file exists so an editor, a CI job or a non-Python consumer can check the shape without reimplementing it, and tests/globus/test_configdoc_schema.py fails if the two ever disagree.

storage_gateways.description: At least one; a document declaring none would reconcile an endpoint to nothing.

collections.description: May be empty: a gateway can be declared before any collection is rooted on it.

roles.description: Endpoint and collection role assignments. Never removed by the reconcile.

display_name.description: Identity for reconciliation. Objects are matched by display name within the endpoint, so changing this creates a second gateway rather than renaming one.

type.description: Only the S3 connector is supported. The POSIX path was removed (ADR 001).

domains.description: Identity domains allowed to use the gateway. Empty would mean no identity could ever use it.

high_assurance.description: Immutable in Globus. The reconcile reports drift here as an error rather than recreating the gateway.

authentication_timeout_mins.description: How long before a human must re-authenticate. There is no 30-day High Assurance ceiling — see ADR 010's Correction.

credential_secret.description: Secrets Manager secret id holding the S3 credential. The secret's VALUE never appears in this document, in Terraform state, or on disk.

credential_identity.description: Globus identity the S3 credential is registered for (`user-credentials s3-create`). Optional: a gateway may be declared before anyone has registered a key against it.

s3_listener.description: The loopback signing listener this gateway is registered against. null for a gateway not yet cut over, which still signs with a static key — `globus doctor` reports that rather than failing. Replaced `iam_user` (retire-globus-s3-access-keys 4.4).

writer_role.description: IAM role NAME the listener signs as, confined to this gateway's prefix. A name rather than an ARN, so the document can be rendered without the account id.

endpoint.description: The --s3-endpoint the gateway was registered with, e.g. https://127.0.0.1:8443. HTTPS only: TLS on loopback is a design decision (D5), not an accident.

managed.description: false means the reconcile reports drift but never applies it. Used to declare production read-only during a rollout.

gateway.description: Display name of a gateway declared in this document. THE REFERENTIAL RULE JSON SCHEMA CANNOT EXPRESS — configdoc.validate() checks it.

base_path.description: Absolute path within the gateway. For S3 the first component is the bucket, which is why the IAM key prefix is this path minus that component.

public.description: Whether the collection is listed publicly in Globus. Defaults CLOSED, which is the opposite of GCS's own default: a declaration that forgets to say should produce the collection that can still be opened, not one already advertised. simplify-globus-ingress 8.8 rebuilt staging from config and got a public collection back.

allow_guest_collections.description: Whether users may create guest collections beneath this one. Production allows it; staging does not.

force_encryption.description: Whether every transfer on this collection must be encrypted. Staging is created with it; production is not.

principal.description: Globus identity or group the role is granted to.

collection.description: Display name of a declared collection. Absent means the role is granted on the endpoint itself. Also referential — checked by configdoc.validate().
